items.title: 61520_Teddy Edwards oral history interview
items.q: I also saw over there people like Butterbeans and Susie.

ctx.x: Dizzy Gillespie -- that hand. Hell, that was a real monster he had there, that particular band.

I also saw over there people like Butterbeans and Susie. Ha-ha, that takes you back, huh? They had ...(?)..., and they had Honi Coles, the great tap dancers there. And Elaine(?) Dixon and [INAUDIBLE NAME]. The great Baby Lawrence, who was probably the greatest tap dancer who ever lived. It's a shame that they didn't get him on film the way that some.... They didn't leave enough of him on film. Because he was... To me he was like the Charlie Parker of dance. I remember I used to see him on Adams and St. Antoine.…

Pete Nugent, a classy dancer. And Kilroy... He was a dancer, a tap dancer. Oh, they had the Groundhog, and Leon Collins. There were so many great performers. Patterson and Jackson, a comedy team; I know you've heard of them. And Bunny Briggs; I first saw Bunny Briggs there. I saw Bill Robinson dance there at the Paradise Theatre. Every week they would change shows, you know.
